description.value: The study examined neural correlates of emotional reactivity and cognitive reappraisal to aversive social imagery across adolescence and young adulthood using fMRI, including age-related activation, mediation, and PPI analyses.

spans.text: we use fMRI to examine the neural correlates of emotional reactivity and reappraisal in response to aversive social imagery in a group of 78 adolescents and young adults aged 15–25 years.

value: we anticipated developmentally mediated linear improvements in the efficiency of reappraisal, either in the form of age‐related increases in prefrontal cortical engagement [McRae et al., 2012 ] and/or age‐related increases in the down‐regulation of amygdala activity [Pitskel et al., 2011 ].

we hypothesized developmental effects in a broader network of neural regions, particularly regions within the “social‐information processing network,” that are associated with social processing and attention to biologically salient visual imagery [Burnett et al., 2011 ; Scherf et al., 2012 ].

This included the left and right primary somatosensory cortex; right dorsal amygdala extending to ventral pallidum and putamen; and secondary visual cortex.

name.value: PPI analysis of task-dependent amygdala-fusiform connectivity

definition.value: Task-dependent increases in functional connectivity strength were observed between the right amygdala and the left fusiform gyrus during “look-negative > reappraise”.

spans.text: The final composition of the sample was 78 participants (44 females), with a mean age of 19.91 years (SD = 2.78; range 15–25, see Supporting Information Fig. 1).

To do so we performed a psychophysiological interactions (PPI) analysis in SPM8 [Friston et al. 1997 ] to assess task‐related changes (“reappraise > look‐negative”) in the functional connectivity of the amygdala as our primary “seed” region of interest (ROI) and the fusiform gyrus and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex as our “target” ROIs.

value: Task-dependent increases in functional connectivity strength were observed between the right amygdala and the left fusiform gyrus during “look-negative > reappraise”. In other words, reappraisal was associated with significant functional decoupling between amygdala and fusiform activity compared to when viewing negative images.

definition.value: Younger age was associated with less amygdala-fusiform decoupling during reappraisal.

The functional sequence consisted of a single shot gradient recalled EPI sequence
A 3T General Electric Signa Excite system

The functional sequence consisted of a single shot gradient recalled EPI sequence in the steady state (repetition time, 2,000 ms; echo time, 35 ms; and pulse angle, 90°) in a 23‐cm field of view, with a 64 × 64‐pixel matrix and a slice thickness of 3.5 mm (no gap).
The total sequence time was 16 min, corresponding to 485 whole brain echo‐planar imaging volumes.
A 3T General Electric Signa Excite system equipped with an 8‐channel phased‐array head coil was used in combination with ASSET parallel imaging (Sunshine Hospital, Western Health, Melbourne).
